transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM), Maya Lopez (Penumbra Head of ML), Tom Richardson (Platform Engineer), Aisha Khan (Procurement), Luis Ortega (SRE)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for carving out time today, um we'll run through where adoption is, cost mechanics and SLA questions, and Priya will do a quick tech read. Maya, do you want to kick off with a quick status?

[00:18] Maya (Penumbra): Sure yeah. So, we've rolled out the recommendation feature to 10% of web traffic, that's been for two weeks, we saw a small bump in conversion which is good. The tricky part is latency on the longer context sessions — some requests hit 800ms to 1.2s and that is, uh, above our target. We're also seeing cost in line with our projection but spikes on peak hours.

[00:40] Tom (Penumbra): To add, our infra team saw that KV cache hit rates vary a lot per user session, we have very bursty tails during promos. We're trying to understand whether batching or locking to Dedicated capacity helps more vs improving cache dimensions.

[01:05] Priya (Redwood SE): Yeah, okay. So quick context — Redwood Dedicated (sometimes folks shorthand as Redwood Dedictated in notes) gives you reserved GPU pools which can flatten p99 and give consistent throughput. There's also config knobs on the KV cache and batching window we can tune; for many e-comms workloads increasing prefix caching and smaller batching windows during bursts keeps tail latency down without blowing up token cost.

[01:38] Luis (SRE): Quick question on private network: we can't expose traffic over public internet for PII-enriched requests. VPC peering is a must, and we're also evaluating an on-prem package for the most sensitive flows. What are the options?

[01:52] Alex (Redwood AE): Right. We offer Redwood Private with VPC peering and on-prem options. For the VPC route we provide a customer-controlled control plane and support KMS integrations. Jordan will follow up on the HLD templates.

[02:10] Jordan (Redwood CSM): Yep I'll share the baseline architecture diagram and a checklist.

[02:25] Aisha (Procurement): From billing perspective we need monthly invoicing and clarity on committed spend vs overage billing. Also SOC 2 Type II evidence and, um, do we have ISO stuff?

[02:40] Alex (Redwood AE): We do provide SOC2 docs; ISO is in process, I think we can share current attestations and the compliance pack. On billing, we have reserved capacity contracts that can be monthly or annual — I'll send options.

[03:02] Priya (Redwood SE): Back to latency — a few concrete things: 1) For your 20–30 token latency-critical responses use a pinned, smaller model variant with quantization; 2) Use prefix KV caching aggressively for user-session prompts; 3) set autoscaling buffer on Dedicated to handle promo bursts. We'll provide example config.

[03:35] Maya (Penumbra): We tried a quantized variant yesterday, results were OK but quality dip on named-entity disambiguation. How much risk is there with quantization?

[03:50] Priya (Redwood SE): There is some quality delta; our Optimize tooling suggests per-workload quant profiles and we can A/B test with canary rollouts. You should hold back critical NER flows for full-precision until we have pass rates on your eval set.

[04:17] Tom (Penumbra): On the economics, our finance team flagged that switching to Dedicated will lower per-token unit cost for steady traffic, but there's an up-front commit. Can you walk numbers vs hosted?

[04:31] Alex (Redwood AE): Sure — topline: hosted is pure variable (pay for tokens), Dedicated is committed with predictable monthly cost and lower per-token CPU/GPU amortized. We'll model a 90-day pilot -- show delta for 6/12 month commit. I'll include a simple spreadsheet.

[04:56] Aisha (Procurement): Are there minimums? Also what about termination terms?

[05:05] Alex (Redwood AE): Minimums depend on the Reserved tier; I'll include the standard MSAs and early-termination language. We can be flexible for pilots.

[05:20] [05:20] Priya (Redwood SE): Quick sidebar — for your API patterns, we noticed a lot of repeated context across calls; prefix caching could recover 20–35% token cost on some endpoints. But it's workload dependent; we need token-level traces.

[05:40] Luis (SRE): We can share traces, but some are redacted for PII. We'll produce synthetic traces that mimic the distribution.

[05:55] Maya (Penumbra): Regarding SLA — what's the realistic uptime guarantee? We need 99.9 for the feature to be considered production critical.

[06:10] Alex (Redwood AE): For Dedicated and Private we offer SLA backstops aligned with 99.9 and above depending on tier. For hosted the SLA is lower. We will share the exact SLA table and the error credits policy.

[06:30] Tom (Penumbra): How do we monitor latency across our routes? Can we integrate with our Datadog?

[06:40] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes Redwood Console (sometimes transcribed as Redwood Consol) exposes per-route token cost and latency metrics and we have tracing hooks that forward spans to existing APMs — Datadog, NewRelic. We'll share the integration docs.

[07:05] Maya (Penumbra): On rollout strategies, we want automatic fallback to a smaller model on degraded infra rather than failing requests. Does Redwood support that?

[07:18] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes — smart routing supports policy-based fallback; you can say route to cheaper/compatible variant on overload. There's also canary and A/B rollouts in the Console.

[07:35] Aisha (Procurement): For contract signoff we need contact at Redwood legal — who's assigned?

[07:45] Alex (Redwood AE): I'll loop in our legal lead and your procurement. I'll cc them in the follow-up.

[08:00] [08:00] Priya (Redwood SE): I want to propose a short technical pilot: 2-week benchmark where we run your most common traffic pattern against Hosted, then against Dedicated with KV cache tuned and a quantized model variant. We'll measure TP95, average cost per request, and quality regressions on your eval prompts.

[08:28] Maya (Penumbra): That sounds reasonable. What's the time/cost to run the benchmark?

[08:35] Priya (Redwood SE): For the benchmark itself Redwood can run it; cost will be minimal and we can absorb as part of onboarding for customers heading toward Dedicated. If we need large GPU burn for synthetic load we might ask for a short allowance but normally it's covered.

[09:00] Tom (Penumbra): Two more technical constraints: 1) We have strict egress limits for tokens that go outside our VPC, 2) We need audit logs with per-token metadata for compliance. Can Redwood provide that?

[09:14] Alex (Redwood AE): Audit logs are part of Private deployments and we can surface per-request meta for compliance; we can discuss retention windows. For egress we'll need to scope which flows remain in VPC vs hosted.

[09:30] Maya (Penumbra): On quantization A/B tests, can you run NER-specific tests? That's the main quality gate for us.

[09:42] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, please send a small eval set focusing on entity disambiguation; we'll run the test and share quality metrics. Keep in mind model variant differences — sometimes smaller quantized variants can be tuned with temperature/penalty to minimize failures.

[10:05] Luis (SRE): A note on networking — if we go VPC peering, how do you handle route failover across regions? Our users are global and we want regional fallbacks.

[10:20] Jordan (Redwood CSM): We can set routing policies by region, and for Dedicated we can provision capacity in multiple regions and have automatic fallback rules. We'll map out options in the HLD.

[10:40] Alex (Redwood AE): Ok let's go through initial timeline and responsibilities. Pilot: scope by next week, run 2-week benchmarking the week after, and then review results and decide commit level.

[11:00] Maya (Penumbra): That timeline works for us, pending procurement review of terms.

[11:15] Aisha (Procurement): We'll need sample invoices and the early termination examples. Also, are there pass-through cloud costs?

[11:27] Alex (Redwood AE): There can be cloud pass-through for certain Private on-prem deployments; for hosted and Dedicated it's baked into the price. I'll itemize those in the pricing sheet.

[11:45] [11:45] Priya (Redwood SE): I'll summarize the recommended config: 1) Dedicated pool with autoscale buffer for promo times, 2) aggressive KV prefix caching and 50–100ms batching window during spikes, 3) quantized smaller variant for non-NER flows; keep high-precision for entity flows with canary tests.

[12:10] Tom (Penumbra): For the KV cache hints, do you support per-customer TTLs? We have sessions that need shorter TTLs for privacy reasons.

[12:22] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes TTLs are configurable per-route; we can set session-based TTL and also redact PII before caching. We'll show sample policies.

[12:40] Maya (Penumbra): Any limitations we should watch for if we move to Dedicated? For example, model upgrades or forced rollouts?

[12:52] Alex (Redwood AE): Model version pinning is supported — you can pin a version to a rollout; upgrades can be scheduled and canaryed. There's no forced model swap without notice; we coordinate major infra upgrades with customers.

[13:12] Luis (SRE): Backup question on KMS — do you support customer-managed keys or only Redwood-managed?

[13:20] Alex (Redwood AE): We support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private deployments and Dedicated depending on contract. We'll clarify in the security pack.

[13:32] Jordan (Redwood CSM): Okay capturing action items. We'll follow up with the architecture HLD, the benchmark plan, the pricing sheet and the compliance pack (SOC2, encryption, ISO notes).

[13:45] Maya (Penumbra): Great. For acceptance criteria — we'll look at TP95 under promo load < 700ms, quality pass rate > 98% on NER eval, and cost per thousand requests reduced by at least 15% versus baseline.

[14:02] Alex (Redwood AE): Noted. We'll aim to deliver the benchmark metrics to match those targets and we'll flag any tradeoffs.

[14:20] Aisha (Procurement): Can we get a draft MSA to review in parallel with the pilot?

[14:30] Alex (Redwood AE): Yes I'll loop legal and share a redline-friendly MSA.

[14:40] Tom (Penumbra): One last thing — competitor question: we've been evaluating ModelServeCo; how do you differentiate on SLO/ops?

[14:50] Priya (Redwood SE): Typical diff is production-first tooling: token-level observability, built-in KV cache, and more flexible deployment modes with predictable economics. We'll put together a short comparison doc.

[15:05] Maya (Penumbra): Ok sounds good. Anything else?

[15:10] Alex (Redwood AE): Quick recap of next steps — I'll send pricing and MSA contacts, Priya will share benchmarks and config notes, Jordan will send the HLD and kickoff calendar. Maya/Tom will supply traces + eval and procurement will review terms.

[15:30] Maya (Penumbra): Thanks everyone.

[15:35] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., Redwood Dedictated, KV cash) and speaker overlaps.

References shared during call: "Penumbra_pilot_requirements_v1.docx" (attendee link), "redwood-benchmarks-2025-06.csv" (to be shared by Priya), pricing sheet template (to be sent by Alex).

End of transcript.
